title: Negative Binomial and Zero-Inflated Negative Binomial Regression by IRLS and EM
text: Many responses applied work counts: number doctor visits, articles published, insurance claims. Poisson regression model natural starting point, forces variance equal mean. Real count data usually overdispersed, variance well mean, often contain zeros Poisson model mean can produce. Ignoring overdispersion gives standard errors small tests reject often; ignoring excess zeros gives poor fit common outcome. Two standard extensions address problems. Negative binomial (NB) regression adds dispersion parameter θ\theta variance can exceed mean. Zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) regression goes treats data mixture two groups: structural zeros, always report zero, NB group, may may . project builds R package nbzinbKnight, fits models without general-purpose optimizer. NB regression fitted iteratively reweighted least squares (IRLS) coefficients, alternated Newton–Raphson θ\theta; ZINB regression fitted EM algorithm whose M-steps IRLS fits. goals implement algorithms correctly, show reproduce established functions MASS::glm.nb() pscl::zeroinfl(), check simulation ZINB estimates standard errors behave , use package analyse physician visits NMES1988 data.

title: Zero-inflated negative binomial regression by EM with IRLS M-steps — zinbreg
text: Fits zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB) model. probability \(\pi_i\) observation structural zero; otherwise comes NB2 distribution mean \(\mu_i\) dispersion \(\theta\). count model \(\log \mu_i = x_i^\top\beta + o_i\) zero model \(\mathrm{logit}\,\pi_i = z_i^\top\gamma\). observed-data log-likelihood maximized EM algorithm: E-step computes posterior probability \(\tau_i\) zero structural, M-steps logistic IRLS fit \(\gamma\) (fractional response \(\tau_i\)) weighted NB fit \((\beta, \theta)\) prior weights \(1 - \tau_i\). general-purpose optimizer used.
